Comments

A comment anchors to whatever it is about — a card, a group, an empty point on the canvas, the board as a whole, or a range of text inside a document. On the canvas each conversation is a small pin at the corner of its card, and the comments button lists them all. Comments thread, resolve, and support @ mentions that notify the person named. A switch in the comments list hides the pins, for you alone, when you want to see the board clean.

Updated November 17, 2026

Comments attach to the thing they are about. This is the whole design: feedback that lives in a sidebar, ordered by time, loses the connection to what it referred to within a day.

What you can comment on

AnchorReads as
A card"this image"
A group"this sequence"
An empty point"something should go here"
The board"the whole thing"
A text range in a document or a note"this sentence"

Right-click a card, a group or the empty canvas and choose the comment item (on a phone, touch and hold), or use the rail's + → Annotate → Comment and click what it is about. A box opens right there, beside the spot its pin will sit on.

A comment on the board as a whole has no place on the canvas, so it has no pin: it shows in the comments list. Those come from the API or an assistant.

Pins on the canvas

Each open conversation is a small pin with the face of whoever started it, sitting at the top-right corner of its card or group, or on its point. Pins stay the same size however far you zoom. Several conversations on one card line up along its top edge.

  • A dot on a pin means there is something in it you haven't read.
  • Zoomed out, pins that would crowd each other gather into one pin with a number. Click it and the board zooms in until they come apart.
  • Point at a pin to read how it begins, who wrote it and when, and how many replies it has.
  • Click a pin to open the conversation in a card beside what it is about. The open pin and its card are ringed in gold.
  • Right-click a pin for its own menu: Open, Resolve (or Reopen), Copy link and Delete.
  • Drag a pin that sits on a point to move it, if you wrote it or can edit the board. A pin on a card or a group follows what it is on.

On a phone or an iPad, tap a pin and the conversation opens as a sheet from the bottom of the screen. A new comment starts in the same sheet; see Mobile and tablet.

Delete a card and its comments go with it; restore the card and they come back.

The comments list

The comments button at the top left of the board shows how many conversations are open, with a dot when one is unread. Press it for the list:

TabHolds
OpenEvery open conversation on the board
ResolvedThe ones that were resolved
For youOpen ones where you were mentioned or replied to

Each row says what the comment is on, who wrote it, when, how it begins and how much was said since. Point at a row to light its card; click it and the board moves there and opens the conversation.

Hiding them

At the bottom of the list is Show comments on the canvas. Turn it off and the pins go, for you only: it changes what you see on this board in this browser, and nothing for anyone else. The list keeps working while they are hidden, and starting a new comment turns them back on. Use it when presenting or when the feedback has piled up and you want to see the work.

Threads

Open a conversation to read it and reply. Enter sends and Shift+Enter starts a new line; on a phone or tablet keyboard, the return key sends, as the send button does.

Resolve when the thing is dealt with. A resolved conversation leaves the canvas and is kept under Resolved in the list, not deleted, so the record of why something changed survives. It says who resolved it; Reopen brings it back, and so does replying to it.

Each comment's ⋯ menu has:

  • Copy link — a link that opens the board, goes to the card and opens the conversation at that comment. If the comment has since been deleted, the link opens the board and says the comment isn't there any more.
  • Edit — on your own comments. An edited comment is marked edited.
  • Delete — a conversation's own ⋯ has Delete conversation, which takes its replies with it.

Resolving and deleting each show a toast with Undo.

Who can do what

Who
Start a comment, replyAnyone who can open the board
Edit a comment's wordsOnly the person who wrote it
Resolve or reopenWhoever started the conversation, and anyone who can edit the board
DeleteThe person who wrote it, and anyone who can edit the board

A reply to a resolved conversation reopens it. If it stays resolved, the reply is still sent and a toast says who can reopen it.

Words you haven't sent

Nothing you type is lost by clicking somewhere else. A comment you started and left keeps a pin of its own where you began it, and pressing that pin brings the words back; an unfinished reply waits in its conversation. Drafts are kept in this browser, for you. Esc in a box with words in it asks Discard this comment? first, with Keep writing as the way back; in an empty box it just closes.

Mentions

Type @ in a comment to mention someone. On the canvas, in a document and in a note, it offers the people who can see the board. The person you name is told, under the bell and by toast, and by email when they are not in the app, and the notice opens that comment. A reply tells everyone who has written in the conversation, a new comment tells the person who made the cluster, and resolving tells whoever started the conversation; nobody is told about their own comment. See Notifications.

Comments on a shared file have no @: the people there may be outside your workspace.

On the words of a note or a document

Select words in a note or a document and comment on them. The words are tinted while their conversation is open for discussion, turn gold while you have it open, and read as plain text again once it is resolved. Click commented words to open their conversation.

A note with comments has a row in its right-click menu that reads like 3 comments: it lists the note's conversations, Open and Resolved. A document lists its own in its side panel; see comments in documents.

Who can comment

On the canvas, anyone who can open the board, including viewers. Editing a card is a different right from talking about it, and feedback is the point of sharing a board with someone. Public links are the exception: they are anonymous, and comments need an account.

A comment on a text range is different: it lives inside the text of the document or note, so it follows edit access. A viewer can open those conversations and read them, but adding, replying to, resolving or deleting one needs edit access.

From your own code, or an assistant

The Comments API lists a board's threads, the ones inside its documents included, and adds, resolves and deletes comments; its page says who may do each. Connected over MCP, an assistant can read the feedback on a board, act on it, reply, resolve what it dealt with, and comment on the words of a document.

Comments versus votes

  • A comment is a sentence: reasoning, a request, a decision, with a thread and a record.
  • A vote is a count: which of these, quickly, with no discussion.

If you want to know why, use a comment.

Frequently asked questions

Can I comment on empty canvas?

Yes. A comment can anchor to a point rather than an object, which is how you leave "something should go here".

How do I hide comments for a presentation?

Open the comments list from the comments button at the top left of the board and turn off Show comments on the canvas. It affects only your view, and the list still has every conversation.

Do resolved comments disappear?

They leave the canvas and are kept under Resolved in the comments list rather than deleted, so the record of a decision survives. Reopen brings one back, and so does a reply.

What happens to a comment I started typing and did not send?

It is kept. Click away and the words wait where you left them, in this browser, and Esc asks before discarding anything you typed.
